standard.title: Select and manipulate for meaning
standard.description: select and manipulate visual conventions, visual arts processes and/or materials to create artworks that represent ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use visual conventions and materials to make artworks that communicate ideas (AC9AVA6C02). They have not yet deliberately selected and manipulated conventions with a clear rationale for how each choice serves the intended meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students select and manipulate visual conventions, processes and materials to create artworks where choices are deliberate and connected to intended ideas, perspectives and meaning.

nodes.label: Making deliberate choices with visual conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make deliberate choices about visual conventions and explain how each choice serves the intended meaning or effect
nodes.minimum_width: Make at least two deliberate convention choices in an artwork; explain how each contributes to the intended meaning or effect
nodes.typical_width: Create an artwork where convention choices are deliberate and documented; explain the reasoning behind each significant choice using visual arts terminology
wider: Experiment with using modulated and directional lines to create a sense of movement — evaluate whether the convention achieves the intended effect and what adjustments are needed
Explore how breaking a rhythmic pattern creates discord — deliberately deploy this in own work and evaluate its expressive impact
Develop an artwork where every major convention choice is documented and justified — use the documentation as a reflective text about own decision-making

response_modes.reason: Students commonly make convention choices by intuition or habit without connecting them to intended meaning — they use familiar conventions because they're comfortable, not because they're the best choice. Working across different convention types and intended effects forces students to develop the habit of purposeful selection rather than defaulting to familiarity.

success_criteria: Makes at least two convention choices that are deliberate and documented
Explains how each choice serves the intended meaning — not just describes the choice
Does not explain choices as 'I like how it looks' without connecting to intended meaning

nodes.label: Working across media and processes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select processes and materials appropriate to their intended meaning and explain why those choices serve the artistic concept better than alternatives
nodes.minimum_width: Select at least one process or material with a clear rationale for why it suits the intended meaning; explain what this choice enables that an alternative would not
nodes.typical_width: Create artworks using selected processes and materials that are connected to intended meaning; evaluate whether material and process choices are serving the concept; document decision-making
wider: Create a work using digital tools (AR assets, photographic manipulation, digital drawing) and evaluate how digital processes extend or constrain expressive possibilities compared to analog approaches
Transform an analog artwork into digital versions and evaluate which transformation best serves the intended meaning — document the decision using visual arts terminology
Consider sustainable design practices as a material constraint — explore sustainable fabrics or recycled materials and evaluate how constraints generate creative possibilities

response_modes.reason: Students commonly select materials and processes based on what they know how to use rather than what serves the intended meaning. Scaffolding the selection reasoning (what does this material allow, what does it prevent, how does that connect to what I'm trying to communicate?) builds the habit of purposeful material thinking rather than defaulting to the familiar.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The digital and analog comparison direction is genuinely rich — students who engage here develop a principled understanding of what different media and processes afford expressively, rather than just technical proficiency. The sustainable materials direction also opens genuine conceptual territory about constraint as creative catalyst.
success_criteria: Selects process or material with a documented rationale connected to intended meaning
Explains what the choice enables that an alternative would not
Material/process choice is connected to concept, not just to familiarity or convenience

nodes.label: Creating artworks that communicate ideas and meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create an artwork where visual convention, process and material choices work together to communicate ideas, perspectives or meaning to an audience
nodes.minimum_width: Create an artwork that realises at least two intended ideas or meanings through deliberate convention, process or material choices
nodes.typical_width: Create an artwork demonstrating consistent and considered selection and manipulation of conventions, processes and materials; reflect on whether the artwork communicates the intended meaning effectively
wider: Create an artwork that explores personal feelings or emotions — evaluate whether the visual choices successfully externalise an internal experience
Create a work (independently or collaboratively) that tells a story or creates awareness about a significant issue — evaluate how visual choices support the communicative intent
Develop an extended artistic practice across a unit using a visual diary — reflect on how convention, process and material choices have evolved as the concept has deepened

response_modes.reason: This node integrates deliberate convention selection (Node 1), purposeful process and material choice (Node 2), and planning/development work from AC9AVA8C01 into a completed artwork. The coordination of all these elements into a coherent communicative whole is the learning — students who can make individual deliberate choices but cannot sustain those choices across a complete work have not reached this node.

success_criteria: Creates an artwork that realises at least two intended ideas or meanings
Convention, process and material choices are deliberate and connected to intended meaning
Can explain what the artwork communicates and how specific choices serve that communication
